intent: A water quiz told as plumbing: the kingdom with no river lifts into view, a WADIS / DESAL split explains where its water does and does not come from, and a pipeline route draws from the Gulf coast to the capital with a water drop riding it inland — the sea, delivered.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which is the BIGGEST country with no rivers?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which is the biggest country with no rivers?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Saudi Arabia. The biggest country with no permanent river or natural lake.

lines.direction: ease back over the peninsula; the Australian flag-ball thinks on 'Australia'; a river sticker on 'Egypt' and a dry-cracked sticker on 'flows' as Saudi Arabia pulses
lines.text: Australia has rivers, some seasonal. Egypt is built on the Nile. Here nothing flows all year.

lines.direction: drift south over the Najd; a rain sticker on 'rain'; the WADIS / DESAL split lands on 'wadis'; a wave sticker on 'sea' as Saudi Arabia pulses
lines.text: Rain comes a few days a year, races down dry valleys called wadis, and is gone. The kingdom makes water from the sea.

lines.direction: tighten on the Gulf coast and the capital; the Jubail pin on 'pumped' as the pipeline route draws inland with a water-drop sticker riding it; the Riyadh pin and the MADE WATER card on 'capital'; the pipe tag; the Saudi flag-ball grins on 'uphill' as Saudi Arabia pulses; the pins leave at the end
lines.text: It is pumped from the Gulf coast across the desert to the capital, hundreds of kilometres inland, uphill.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: It drinks the sea. Follow us.
